oneTimers: A one-time, non-cash income tax charge of $10.2B sits inside the $14.9B tax line — fallout from the European General Court overturning the State Aid decision on Apple's Irish tax arrangements. It does not reflect the quarter's trading: income before taxes rose 10% to $29.6B.

segments.name: Mac

segments.name: iPad
segments.note: Tablets — the redesigned iPad Pro and iPad Air drove an 8% rise.

segments.note: Apple Watch, AirPods and home devices — down 3% against a tough comparison.

segments.name: Services
segments.note: App Store, Apple Music, iCloud, TV+ and advertising — an all-time record, up 12%.

takeaways.text: A European court decision on Apple's Irish taxes forced a one-time, non-cash tax charge of $10.2B. Reported EPS fell to $0.97 — without the charge it would have been about $1.64, and pre-tax profit actually rose 10%.
takeaways.title: A one-off tax charge drove the headline

takeaways.text: Services revenue reached $25.0B, an all-time high, up 12% — more than a quarter of everything Apple sells now comes from subscriptions, the App Store and other services.
takeaways.title: Services hit another record

takeaways.text: iPhone sales rose 6% to $46.2B — about $49 of every $100 Apple took in — as the iPhone 16 launch landed in the final weeks of the quarter.
takeaways.title: iPhone still carries the quarter

verdict: Apple grew sales 6% to $94.9B on record Services revenue, but a one-time $10.2B European tax charge cut reported profit to $14.7B — without it, profit would have been about $24.9B.
